blocks.charleston|car-accident-lawyers:
Charleston County recorded 16,118 collisions in 2023, the second-highest total of any county in South Carolina, and US-17 alone accounted for 1,942 of them. A peninsula crash frequently involves a visitor, a rideshare driver or a delivery vehicle rather than a neighbour, which changes which policies apply and who the real defendant is.

We investigate independently rather than accepting the adjuster's reconstruction, and we identify every available policy — including stacked uninsured and underinsured coverage — before any offer is evaluated.
blocks.charleston|truck-accident-lawyers:
Container traffic from the Columbus Street and Hugh Leatherman terminals moves through Charleston streets to reach I-26, and a crash involving one is rarely a single-defendant case. The driver, the motor carrier, the trailer owner, a broker and whoever loaded and sealed the container may each bear responsibility, each with separate coverage.

These claims are decided on the carrier's electronic records — logging device data, engine control module downloads, maintenance and driver-qualification files — all subject to short federal retention periods under 49 C.F.R. We demand preservation immediately.
blocks.charleston|motorcycle-accident-lawyers:
Charleston's peninsula streets combine narrow lanes, heavy turning movements and drivers unfamiliar with the grid, and the recurring motorcycle crash is a vehicle turning across a rider's path. Proving it takes sight-line and closing-speed evidence, because the driver's account is almost always that the motorcycle appeared from nowhere.

Adjusters also arrive assuming rider fault. South Carolina requires helmets only under 21, so an adult riding without one has broken no law — the helmet becomes an argument about comparative fault and injury causation, answered with medical evidence.
blocks.charleston|workers-compensation-lawyers:
Your employer's insurance carrier is not neutral and does not represent you. Charleston claims frequently arise from hospitality, port and construction work, where injuries are attributed to pre-existing conditions and light-duty offers are used to cut off temporary benefits early.

We file the claim correctly, contest denials before the South Carolina Workers' Compensation Commission, press for an appropriate treating physician and an accurate impairment rating, and pursue any third-party claim that runs alongside the compensation case rather than being absorbed by it.
blocks.charleston|personal-injury-lawyers:
Charleston claims are shaped by who is involved. A significant share of serious injuries here happen to people who do not live in South Carolina, which raises the question of which policies apply and whether an out-of-state insurer is entitled to interpret South Carolina coverage on its own terms.

The rest is discipline: proving fault precisely enough to withstand a comparative-fault reduction, and documenting the injury consistently from the first medical visit, because gaps in treatment are the most common lever used to discount a claim.
blocks.charleston|slip-and-fall-lawyers:
A premises case turns on notice — whether the owner knew about the hazard or should have found it. That is rarely proved by the fall itself, but by maintenance logs, inspection schedules, prior complaints about the same hazard, and the property's own incident report.

Surveillance is the half that disappears. Many hospitality and retail systems overwrite within fourteen to thirty days, and no law compels otherwise. A preservation demand sent promptly is often the difference between having the footage and arguing about what it would have shown.
blocks.charleston|premises-liability-lawyers:
Charleston's tourism economy means many premises injuries happen to guests at hotels, restaurants and historic properties whose owners carry substantial coverage and retain counsel quickly. Liability may sit with the operator, a management company, a maintenance contractor or the building owner, and each will look to the others.

What decides these cases is notice: proving the hazard existed long enough that a reasonable owner should have found it. Inspection records, prior complaints and surveillance all speak to that, and all have to be demanded early.
blocks.charleston|wrongful-death-lawyers:
South Carolina splits a fatal-injury case in two. The wrongful death action belongs to the statutory beneficiaries; the survival action belongs to the estate and covers what the person suffered before death. Both must be brought by a personal representative appointed through probate, and that appointment has to happen before either claim can proceed.

We handle the probate step alongside the claim, so the case is not delayed by an administrative prerequisite, and we work with economists to value a lifetime of lost support rather than accepting a policy-limits figure.
blocks.charleston|brain-injury-lawyers:
The most consequential brain injuries are the ones missed at the emergency department. A patient who is alert and oriented after a crash is frequently discharged with a normal CT scan, and the cognitive, memory and personality changes emerge over weeks — by which point the medical record shows a minor injury.

Closing that gap requires neuropsychological testing, treating-physician documentation and testimony from people who knew the client before, not just imaging. MUSC is the state's only Adult and Paediatric Level I trauma centre, and its records are usually central.
blocks.charleston|spinal-cord-injury-lawyers:
A spinal cord injury is valued on a lifetime, not a treatment episode. Attendant care, home and vehicle modification, durable equipment replacement cycles, and lost earning capacity together dwarf the immediate hospital bill, and none of it appears in a medical-records summary.

We work with life-care planners and economists to build that projection properly, and we resolve health-insurance and Medicaid liens before settlement so the figure the client is offered resembles the figure they actually receive.
blocks.charleston|burn-injury-lawyers:
Burn cases are valued differently from other catastrophic injuries because the harm continues after the medical treatment ends. Scarring, contracture, repeated reconstructive surgery and permanent disfigurement carry damages that are real but resist the formulas insurers prefer to apply.

Liability often reaches beyond the immediate cause to a product manufacturer, a property owner who ignored a known fire hazard, or a contractor who installed a system incorrectly. Preserving the scene and the failed component early is what keeps those defendants in the case.
blocks.charleston|medical-malpractice-lawyers:
South Carolina makes a malpractice case harder to start than an ordinary injury claim. Before filing, a claimant must serve a Notice of Intent and an expert affidavit identifying at least one negligent act, and the case then goes to pre-suit mediation. The statute of limitations is also its own — S.C. Code § 15-3-545, not the general three-year rule.

Those prerequisites take time to satisfy properly, which is why a malpractice case should be evaluated long before the deadline appears close.
blocks.charleston|nursing-home-abuse-lawyers:
Nursing home cases are won on documents the facility controls: staffing rosters, care plans, wound-assessment records, incident reports and DHEC survey history. A family sees the injury; the record shows whether the facility was chronically understaffed on the shifts that mattered.

Many admission agreements also contain an arbitration clause signed at a moment of crisis, sometimes by a relative without legal authority to bind the resident. Whether that clause is enforceable is frequently the first fight, and it is worth having.
blocks.charleston|dog-bite-lawyers:
South Carolina does not require a prior bite. Under S.C. Code § 47-3-110 an owner is strictly liable when a dog attacks someone lawfully in a place they are entitled to be, so the case usually turns on the victim's conduct and location rather than the animal's history.

Recovery normally comes from a homeowner's or renter's policy, which means identifying the correct policy and any breed exclusion early. Children are disproportionately the victims and disproportionately injured to the face, where scarring damages are substantial.
blocks.charleston|pedestrian-accident-lawyers:
Pedestrian claims start with an assumption of fault against the person on foot, particularly downtown at night. Right of way under S.C. Code § 56-5 depends on the crossing, the signal and the lighting, and reconstructing it requires the scene rather than the driver's account.

Where a driver flees or carries minimum limits — common in these cases — uninsured motorist coverage on the pedestrian's own policy frequently becomes the primary source of recovery, and it applies even though they were not in a vehicle.
blocks.charleston|bicycle-accident-lawyers:
Charleston's cycling volume, narrow peninsula streets and heavy on-street parking produce a specific crash pattern: a driver opening a door into a rider's path, or turning across a bike lane. Insurers reflexively argue the cyclist was where they should not have been, so establishing lane position and right of way early matters.

As with pedestrian claims, a cyclist's own uninsured and underinsured motorist coverage usually applies, and it is often the largest available source when the driver carries minimum limits.
blocks.charleston|electric-scooter-accident-law:
Scooter cases turn on coverage that often does not exist. A rented scooter is not covered by an auto policy, the rental operator's terms attempt to disclaim liability, and the rider may have no applicable insurance at all — which pushes recovery toward the at-fault driver, the operator's own coverage, or a defective-equipment claim.

We establish which of those applies before the claim is framed, because the answer determines who the defendant is and what has to be preserved.
blocks.charleston|golf-cart-accident-lawyers:
Golf carts are street-legal in South Carolina only within limits. Under S.C. Code § 56-2-100 a permitted cart may operate in daylight, within four miles of the owner's registered address, on roads posted 35 mph or less, and only with a licensed driver. Operation outside those limits supports a negligence-per-se argument.

Coverage is the practical problem: many carts are uninsured, and recovery often depends on a homeowner's policy, a rental operator's coverage, or the injured person's own uninsured motorist protection.
blocks.charleston|boating-accident-lawyers:
A boating case runs on a different evidentiary track. SCDNR investigates rather than a police department, there is no scene to preserve once the vessels move, and witnesses are frequently passengers with their own interests. Where the water is navigable, federal maritime law may displace parts of South Carolina law entirely.

We establish the applicable law first, obtain the SCDNR file, and identify whether a vessel owner, an operator, a rental company or a manufacturer is the right defendant.
blocks.charleston|maritime-injury-lawyers:
Which statute covers a maritime injury decides almost everything about it, and the categories are narrow. A seaman injured aboard a vessel proceeds under the Jones Act; a longshore or terminal worker proceeds under the LHWCA, which carries a one-year deadline under 33 U.S.C. § 913 and a very different benefits structure.

Misclassifying the claim can forfeit it. With the Port of Charleston immediately at hand, we establish status and coverage at the outset rather than after a deadline has run.
blocks.charleston|product-liability-lawyers:
A product case can be brought on a defective design, a manufacturing flaw, or an inadequate warning, and which theory applies determines what has to be proved and which experts are needed.

The single most decisive step is early: preserving the product itself, unaltered, along with its packaging, manuals and purchase record. Once a vehicle is repaired or a failed component discarded, the case usually goes with it — and manufacturers know that.
blocks.charleston|construction-accident-lawyers:
Workers' compensation is the exclusive remedy against your employer, but it is rarely the only claim available on a construction site. A general contractor, a subcontractor, an equipment manufacturer, a property owner or an engineer may each bear liability outside the compensation system, and those claims carry damages compensation does not — including pain and suffering.

We pursue both tracks together, and move quickly on site conditions, OSHA findings and equipment before the site changes.

Freight reaches the Grand Strand on SC-22 and US-501, two corridors that fail in opposite ways: the Conway Bypass at highway speed across bridge sections with no shoulder, and US-501 through congested signalised commercial frontage.

Either way the defendant is usually a carrier rather than a driver, and the case is decided on records the carrier holds — logging device data, engine control module downloads, maintenance and driver-qualification files — subject to short federal retention periods. We demand preservation immediately.
blocks.myrtle-beach|motorcycle-accident-lawyers:
US-17 through the Grand Strand mixes riders with unfamiliar seasonal drivers making frequent turns into commercial frontage, and the recurring crash is a vehicle turning across a rider's path. Proving it requires sight-line and closing-speed evidence rather than the driver's account.

Insurers begin from an assumption of rider fault. South Carolina requires helmets only under 21, so an adult riding without one has broken no law; the helmet becomes a comparative-fault and causation argument.
blocks.myrtle-beach|workers-compensation-lawyer:
The Grand Strand's hospitality and construction employers generate seasonal and transient workforces, and compensation carriers routinely dispute whether a worker was an employee at all — or push a light-duty offer that ends temporary benefits early.

We establish employment status, file correctly, contest denials before the South Carolina Workers' Compensation Commission, press for an accurate impairment rating, and pursue any third-party claim alongside the compensation case.
blocks.myrtle-beach|personal-injury-lawyers:
A large share of serious Grand Strand injuries happen to people who do not live here, which creates two practical problems: treatment begins locally and continues in another state, leaving a fragmented medical record, and the policies that matter are frequently out of state.

South Carolina law governs regardless of where the injured person lives, and it permits stacking of uninsured and underinsured coverage — often worth considerably more than an out-of-state insurer's first assessment suggests.
blocks.myrtle-beach|slip-and-fall-lawyers:
Hotels, restaurants and attractions along the Grand Strand carry substantial coverage and retain counsel quickly, and their surveillance is the evidence that decides these cases — and the evidence that disappears. Many systems overwrite within fourteen to thirty days.

Notice is the element: proving the hazard existed long enough that a reasonable operator should have found it. Inspection logs, prior complaints and the incident report all speak to it, and all must be demanded promptly.
blocks.myrtle-beach|premises-liability-lawyers:
Grand Strand premises claims frequently involve a guest injured at a property whose operator, management company, maintenance contractor and owner are four different entities, each pointing at the others while the evidence ages.

Notice resolves it — proving the condition existed long enough that a reasonable owner should have discovered it. Inspection records, prior complaints about the same hazard and surveillance are the proof, and all are routinely discarded on a short cycle.
blocks.myrtle-beach|wrongful-death-lawyers:
South Carolina divides a fatal-injury case in two: a wrongful death action for the statutory beneficiaries, and a survival action belonging to the estate for what the person suffered before death. Both require a personal representative appointed through probate first.

Where the family lives out of state — common on the Grand Strand — that appointment still happens in South Carolina. We handle it alongside the claim so the case is not delayed by an administrative prerequisite.
blocks.myrtle-beach|brain-injury-lawyers:
The brain injuries that matter most are missed on the first day. A patient who is alert with a normal CT is discharged, and the memory, concentration and personality changes emerge over weeks — leaving a record that describes a minor injury.

Closing that gap takes neuropsychological testing and testimony from people who knew the client before. Grand Strand Medical Center is the region's Adult Level I trauma centre; where a patient was first stabilised at a Level III or IV facility, both sets of records matter.
blocks.myrtle-beach|spinal-cord-injury-lawyers:
A spinal cord injury has to be valued across a lifetime rather than a hospital stay. Attendant care, home and vehicle modification, equipment replacement cycles and lost earning capacity dominate the real cost, and none of it appears in a records summary.

We build that projection with life-care planners and economists, and resolve health-insurance and Medicaid liens before settlement so the figure offered resembles the figure received.
blocks.myrtle-beach|burn-injury-lawyers:
Burn injuries keep causing harm after treatment ends — scarring, contracture, repeated reconstructive surgery and permanent disfigurement carry damages that resist the formulas insurers apply.

Liability frequently reaches past the immediate cause to a product manufacturer, a property owner who ignored a known hazard, or a contractor who installed a system wrongly. Preserving the scene and the failed component early keeps those defendants in the case.
blocks.myrtle-beach|medical-malpractice-lawyers:
A South Carolina malpractice case is harder to start than an ordinary claim. Before filing, a claimant must serve a Notice of Intent with an expert affidavit identifying a negligent act, and the case then goes to pre-suit mediation. The deadline is its own — S.C. Code § 15-3-545 — not the general three-year rule.

Satisfying those prerequisites properly takes time, which is why a malpractice claim should be evaluated well before the deadline is in sight.
blocks.myrtle-beach|nursing-home-abuse-lawyers:
These cases are won on records the facility controls: staffing rosters, care plans, wound assessments, incident reports and DHEC survey history. A family sees the injury; the record shows whether the facility was understaffed on the shifts that produced it.

Admission agreements also routinely contain arbitration clauses signed during a crisis, sometimes by a relative with no authority to bind the resident. Whether that clause holds is often the first fight and worth having.
blocks.myrtle-beach|dog-bite-lawyers:
South Carolina imposes strict liability under S.C. Code § 47-3-110: no prior bite is required, and an owner is liable when a dog attacks someone lawfully where they are entitled to be.

On the Grand Strand these claims frequently involve a vacation rental, which raises whether the homeowner's policy covers a property in short-term commercial use, and whether the rental platform or property manager carries coverage of its own. Identifying the right policy early is the whole game.
blocks.myrtle-beach|pedestrian-accident-lawyers:
Pedestrian claims begin with an assumption of fault against the person on foot, and on the Grand Strand that assumption is compounded by unfamiliar visitors crossing multi-lane arterials with long gaps between marked crossings.

Right of way under S.C. Code § 56-5 depends on the specific location and signal. Where a driver flees or carries minimum limits, uninsured motorist coverage on the pedestrian's own policy frequently becomes the primary recovery.
blocks.myrtle-beach|bicycle-accident-lawyers:
Grand Strand cycling is heavily seasonal and heavily recreational, which means riders unfamiliar with the roads sharing them with drivers unfamiliar with the area. Insurers reflexively argue the cyclist was where they should not have been, so establishing lane position and right of way early is decisive.

A cyclist's own uninsured and underinsured motorist coverage usually applies, and is frequently the largest source available against a minimum-limits driver.
blocks.myrtle-beach|electric-scooter-accident-l:
Rented scooters are common along the beachfront and rarely covered by anything. An auto policy does not extend to them, the rental operator's terms attempt to disclaim liability, and a visiting rider may carry no applicable insurance at all.

That pushes recovery toward the at-fault driver, the operator's own coverage, or a defective-equipment claim against the rental fleet. We establish which applies before framing the claim.
blocks.myrtle-beach|golf-cart-accident-lawyers:
Golf carts are a genuine feature of Grand Strand traffic rather than a novelty. Under S.C. Code § 56-2-100 a permitted cart may operate only in daylight, within four miles of the owner's registered address, on roads posted 35 mph or less, and with a licensed driver — limits routinely exceeded by vacation renters who were never told them.

Operation outside those limits supports negligence per se, and opens claims against the rental operator as well as the driver.
blocks.myrtle-beach|boating-accident-lawyers:
Grand Strand waters carry heavy recreational and charter traffic, and a boating claim runs on different evidence from a road case. SCDNR investigates rather than a police department, the scene disappears as soon as the vessels move, and witnesses are usually passengers with interests of their own.

Alcohol is a recurring factor. We obtain the SCDNR file promptly and identify whether the owner, operator, charter company or manufacturer is the correct defendant.
blocks.myrtle-beach|maritime-injury-lawyers:
Which statute governs a maritime injury decides nearly everything about it. A seaman proceeds under the Jones Act; a harbour or dock worker proceeds under the LHWCA, which carries a one-year deadline under 33 U.S.C. § 913 and an entirely different benefits structure.

Charter crew, commercial fishing crew and dock workers along the coast fall on different sides of that line. Misclassifying the claim can forfeit it, so status and coverage are established at the outset.
blocks.myrtle-beach|product-liability-lawyers:
A product claim may rest on defective design, a manufacturing flaw or an inadequate warning, and the theory determines what must be proved and which experts are needed.

The decisive step is early and physical: preserving the product unaltered, with its packaging, manuals and purchase record. Once a vehicle is repaired or a failed component discarded, the case usually goes with it.
blocks.myrtle-beach|construction-accident-lawye:
Compensation is the exclusive remedy against your employer, but on a Grand Strand construction site — where resort and residential building runs year-round — it is rarely the only claim. A general contractor, subcontractor, equipment manufacturer or property owner may bear liability outside that system, carrying damages compensation does not.

We pursue both together and move quickly on site conditions, OSHA findings and equipment before the site changes.
blocks.myrtle-beach|atv-side-by-side-accident-l:
Off-road vehicle cases sit outside the assumptions that govern car crashes. There is often no auto policy, no police reconstruction and no scene remaining, and liability may rest with a landowner, a rental operator, an event organiser or the manufacturer rather than another driver.

Rentals are common along the coast, which raises whether the operator's waiver is enforceable and whether the machine was maintained. Preserving it unaltered is the most important early step.
